html:
The November Uprising was a revolt against Russian rule that began in Warsaw on 29 November 1830, when young officer cadets attacked the palace of the Russian viceroy, and grew into a war that lasted until October 1831.

The Kingdom of Poland, created after Napoleon, had its own army and parliament under the tsar, but Russia ignored its rights. In January 1831 the Polish parliament deposed Tsar Nicholas I as king. The Polish army fought well at first but lacked leaders and allies, and Warsaw fell in September 1831. Russia ended the kingdom's autonomy and closed its universities. Thousands of Poles, among them the poet Mickiewicz's circle and Chopin, lived in Paris in what was called the Great Emigration. The next great rising was the January Uprising of 1863.
